sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: OmniRoute is a self-hosted AI gateway that routes requests to many model providers through one OpenAI-compatible endpoint. You connect your own provider accounts, including free tiers, and it picks a route and fails over when one runs out.
sixtySeconds.problem: Using several AI providers means juggling SDKs, keys and rate limits, and free tiers run out at different times. OmniRoute puts them behind one local endpoint with quota-aware routing and fallback.
whoFor: Developers who want one endpoint for many AI providers
People using Claude Code, Cursor or Cline with cheaper models
Hobbyists making the most of provider free tiers
Teams that want local control over AI routing
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you want to combine your own provider accounts behind one endpoint with automatic fallback. You still need eligible accounts; the README is clear its token figures are estimates of third-party free tiers, not a grant from OmniRoute.
requirements: Accounts or API keys for the providers you connect

overview: OmniRoute runs on your machine or server and exposes an OpenAI-compatible API at http://localhost:20128/v1. You connect providers in its dashboard with your own accounts or keys, then point any app, IDE or coding agent at that one endpoint.

Combos and quota-aware scheduling route each request to an eligible provider and fall back when one hits a limit. The README catalogs hundreds of providers, many marked free, and re-audits its free-tier estimates every two weeks. Providers whose terms OmniRoute flags as ones to avoid are excluded from automatic routing.
It runs from npm, Docker, from source, or even on a phone through Termux. A headless mode runs only the proxy. It can also be exposed over MCP, A2A, a REST API, webhooks or a remote CLI.
